clue.text: Stew of gar, skate, dabs — a fine kettle of fish!

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble cooked together, so the following words are thrown in and mixed up

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's medley of gar, skate and dabs stewed together turns out a fine mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal; the 'of' after it is part of the fodder, supplying the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a muddle or botched mess, a dog's breakfast being the British slang version.

clue.text: What Hillary didn't do, and what 9 19D insists he doesn't have?

definitions.meaning: Hillary Clinton stayed married to her husband Bill rather than leave him
the EU's Brexit negotiator said there was no exit payment, only a settling of accounts

explanation.surface: A political riddle linking Hillary Clinton's marriage with the EU's Brexit negotiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 19D is Michel Barnier, the EU's chief Brexit negotiator in 2017, who insisted the UK's payment was a settlement of accounts, not a bill for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way it is a legal parting from a husband named Bill; read the other it is the Brexit exit payment.

clue.text: Key for government apartment

parts.note: a flat is the British word for an apartment

explanation.surface: A key to a council-owned flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical key, the major or minor scale built on that note.

clue.text: Scruffy, barelegged leaving European soil

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy and disordered, telling us to jumble the letters
leaving says a letter departs from the jumbled word

explanation.surface: A scruffy, barelegged figure walks out of Europe onto foreign soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scruffy' and 'leaving' together say: rearrange BARELEGGED with one E removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedraggle is to make dirty and wet, so it is a verb synonym of soil.

clue.text: Brooking no dissent, issue red cards, dismissing wingers

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the flanks, so the outer letters of the phrase are dropped

parts.note: a referee who issues red cards will send off players

explanation.surface: A football referee tolerates no argument, sending players off and getting rid of the wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of' is British slang said to close an argument: 'and that's the end of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to shut down debate, the slang tag signals that no further disagreement will be heard.

clue.text: Playful little Christopher; born late summer 2007, I think

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
a child born then was ten years old when this puzzle appeared in 2017
the suffix -ish is used informally to mean roughly or so I believe

explanation.surface: A proud parent describing a lively little boy born in August 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittenish describes someone frisky and frolicsome, like a young cat at play.

clue.text: Turkish commander in range

definitions.meaning: an Ottoman military officer or chief bore this title
a range here is a kitchen stove, and this is a well-known British brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer within firing distance.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a Turkish title for a commander, the other a cast-iron cooking stove.

clue.text: Can print old-fashioned photograph

parts.note: a can is a tin
type is printed lettering

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone can print an antique photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype is a Victorian photograph printed directly onto a thin sheet of iron.

clue.text: I belch drunkenly, getting stuck into liqueur, ignoring grand Frenchman

indicators.note: getting stuck into says the jumbled letters go inside the trimmed liqueur
ignoring says the following word is left out of the liqueur's name

parts.note: Grand Marnier is a French orange liqueur

indicators.note: drunkenly says the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker hiccups while working through a bottle of orange liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand Marnier without GRAND is MARNIER; the anagram of I BELCH goes inside it after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel Barnier is a French politician, the EU's chief Brexit negotiator in 2017.

clue.text: Batting helmet protecting Virginia declared ineffective

indicators.note: protecting says the first pieces surround and shelter the state abbreviation

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
lid is slang for a helmet or hat
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A cricketer's helmet failed to protect a player from Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract or ticket ruled to have no legal force is invalid.

clue.text: Delaware coach to go off the rails

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A Delaware sports coach is about to lose control.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to step off a railway carriage, literally leaving the rails behind.

clue.text: Rocky the Bear leaves

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaky, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer called Rocky the Bear walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is a plural noun: infusions are made from dried leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is brewed from dried leaves of plants such as mint or camomile.

clue.text: Where there's no stopping Spooner's little brawl?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was famed for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: wee is Scots for little
a fray is a brawl or scuffle

explanation.surface: Asking where a small scuffle can't be halted.
explanation.definitionFit: An American motorway is built for continuous traffic without junction stops or signals.

clue.text: Only Fianna. Every time

parts.note: Fianna Fail is an Irish political party; just its first word is the party's name lacking the second word

explanation.surface: A curt note about one Irish political party, then a firm promise.
explanation.walkthrough: Fianna Fáil is a major Irish political party. Read the answer as a direction and Fianna Fáil loses its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something each and every occasion means doing it reliably, never once missing.

clue.text: Noble home of Belgian Standard

definitions.meaning: a feudal lord to whom vassals owed allegiance
Standard is a Belgian football club based in this city

explanation.surface: A nobleman's house flies the Belgian flag.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a feudal lord; the other is the Belgian city whose football club is Standard.

clue.text: For one day only, English pub on green closing early

parts.note: PH, for public house, marks a pub on British maps

indicators.note: closing early says the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: emerald is a bright green

explanation.surface: An English pub on the village green opens for a single day and shuts early.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral comes from the Greek for lasting a day, hence fleeting or short-lived.

clue.text: Doctor Who legs it, getting the message from Johnson

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doctor Who runs away, having got a message from someone named Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2017 Boris Johnson, then Foreign Secretary, said the EU could 'go whistle' for its Brexit divorce money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone they will not get what they want, as Johnson told Brussels.

clue.text: Contemptuous comic disheartened 22

parts.note: a wit is a comic person

indicators.note: disheartened says the heart of the fish's name, one middle letter, is removed

parts.note: the answer at 22 across is a pickled fillet of this fish

explanation.surface: A dispirited comedian is scornful about a pickled fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A withering look or remark is scornful and crushing.

clue.text: British Tory established to be most clever

parts.note: Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A British Conservative set up to be the cleverest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightest means most intelligent, the superlative of bright in its sense of quick-witted.

clue.text: See 9
Yahoo hacks involving something of a fuss

indicators.note: involving says the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Hackers breaking into Yahoo cause a bit of a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a commotion or to-do, a fuss made over something.

clue.text: A jolly girl in the Spanish navy

parts.note: a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful young woman serving in the Spanish navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armada was the fleet Spain sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Bread to soak up pickled fish

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
to mop is to soak up liquid

explanation.surface: Using bread to mop up the juices from pickled fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a fillet of herring rolled around onion and pickled in vinegar.

clue.text: Iron the newspapers

definitions.meaning: to smooth clothes with a hot iron

explanation.surface: Ironing the newspapers, as a butler once did.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to flatten creases with heat, the other the collective name for journalists.

clue.text: Require art room regularly for core community project

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: An instruction to book the art room routinely for a central community scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' is a pun: Euratom is the European Atomic Energy Community, concerned with nuclear cores.
explanation.definitionFit: Euratom is the European body set up to develop nuclear energy, a nuclear community project.

clue.text: Discharge reported from French Inspector's chamber?

indicators.note: reported says we need the spoken version of the word

parts.note: Inspector Clouseau of the Pink Panther films famously says the word for chamber in his mangled accent

explanation.surface: A discharge noted from a French police inspector's office.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Clouseau, Peter Sellers' bumbling French detective, pronounces 'room' as 'rheum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Dip partly responsible for swimmer's ear?

indicators.note: partly responsible for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is a swim the cause of a swimmer's ear infection?
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse something is to plunge or submerge it in liquid.

clue.text: Non-PC elderly farmer blanks Trump

indicators.note: blanks means ignores or snubs, so the name is left out

parts.note: Old MacDonald is the farmer of the nursery song
Donald is Trump's first name

explanation.surface: A politically incorrect old farmer cold-shoulders Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-PC' looks like 'not politically correct', but it means not a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's Mac is the main personal computer rival to the Windows PC.

clue.text: Crystal meth network finally captured in the country

parts.note: ice is street slang for crystal methamphetamine
LAN is a local area network

indicators.note: finally says take the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A crystal meth ring finally caught in the provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Translate Merkel's cables to convey German opinion of May's snap election?

indicators.note: to convey means to carry, so the jumbled letters carry a letter within them
translate means render in different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomatic cables from Angela Merkel reveal what Germany thought of Theresa May's 2017 snap election.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May called a snap UK general election in 2017 and lost her majority.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, ill-judged risk is how a critic might judge an election called needlessly early.
